name: ClockClock 24
description:
ClockClock 24 – White consists of a handcrafted housing of mineral composite and electronic components. It is built on proprietary technology—in both software and hardware—which a team of in-house designers, engineers, and programmers has continuously developed since its inception. The objects are carefully hand-assembled at the studio in Stockholm.

The work was first launched in 2008 as The Clock Clock and exhibited at the Saatchi Gallery in London in 2010. Later, it was reissued as ClockClock 24 in partnership with the MoMA store in New York. Today, it is represented in the permanent collections of the Vitra Design Museum in Germany, the Musée International d'Horlogerie in Switzerland, and the Nationalmuseum in Sweden, among others.

name: ClockClock 24
description:

Drawing inspiration from the richness of Indian culture and the vibrant spirit of Holi, this edition introduces a refined accent of cobalt blue—an homage to celebration and color—set against the serene Scandinavian snow-white case. Sterling hands complete the composition.

It is built on proprietary technology—in both software and hardware—which a team of in-house designers, engineers, and programmers has continuously developed since its inception.

Later, it was reissued as ClockClock 24 in partnership with the MoMA store in New York. Today, it is represented in the permanent collections of the Vitra Design Museum in Germany, the Musée International d'Horlogerie in Switzerland, and the Nationalmuseum in Sweden, among others.

name: ClockClock 24
description:
Humans since 1982 are proudly collaborating with BIG - Bjarke Ingels Group - and SolidNature to create a new series of kinetic timepieces that unite architectural vision, material mastery and precision technology.

Limited to just 10 pieces, this edition is made from Sunset Dune Travertine, handpicked by Bjarke Ingels for the way it captures time within its materiality.

The collaboration grew from Bjarke Ingels’ own collection of Humans since 1982’s work and a shared belief in art’s ability to elevate architectural space. Together, we conceived a series where time is embodied not only through movement and technology but also through material.

Travertine, a stone formed over hundreds of thousands of years, becomes a living canvas for our signature clock hand choreographies. Its layered stratas act as a geological clock, fusing millennia with hours and minutes. Each edition of ClockClock 24 - Bjarke Ingels Sunset Dune is hand-crafted in natural materials, its unique layering and texture ensure no two artworks are entirely alike.

The stone artwork body is combined with Humans since 1982’s proprietary technology, refined by our in-house designers, engineers and programmers since 2009. Each piece is meticulously hand-assembled in our Stockholm studio.

name: ClockClock 24
description:
Kit Kemp Design Studio and Humans since 1982 have collaborated to create a striking new ClockClock 24 edition. Both a kinetic sculpture and a functioning wall clock, embodying both analogue and digital elements the ClockClock 24 - Dada Blue is a mesmerising ode to the passing of time.

ClockClock 24 - Dada Blue consists of a handcrafted housing of mineral composite and electronic components. It is built on proprietary technology—in both software and hardware—which a team of in-house designers, engineers, and programmers has continuously developed since its inception. The objects are carefully hand-assembled at the studio in Stockholm.

The roots of this project reach back to 2008 when the first edition was launched as The Clock Clock, and later exhibited at the Saatchi Gallery in London in 2010. In 2016 it was reissued as ClockClock 24 in partnership with the MoMA store in New York. Today, artworks of this series are represented in the permanent collections of the Vitra Design Museum in Germany, the Musée International d'Horlogerie in Switzerland, and the Nationalmuseum in Sweden, among others.

name: A million Times 61c
description:
A million Times 61c (Tidal) is crafted and milled from a single block of aluminium, coated in dark blue, and features shiny metal finish clock hands. The series is evocative of sunlight reflecting on the surface of water, while the cyclical and cumulative patterns shown by the clock-hands are themselves wave-like, a constant ebb and flow between reporting the time each minute.

The artwork is hand-assembled in our Stockholm studio and is part of a highly limited edition of just 10 pieces.

The first A million Times installation was exhibited in 2013 at the design fairs in Dubai and Basel. Since then artworks from this series have been included in internationally significant exhibitions at the Somerset House (UK), Smithsonian Design Museum (US), Issey Miyake's museum "21_21 Design Sight" (JP) and many more.
